method.scoring: Each Article is scored 0-2 against the subject's own published documents. Every non-zero score MUST carry at least one verbatim quote that verifiably appears in a file under evidence/. Any reader can re-run scoreboard_verify.py to check.

scale.2: Explicitly addressed in a binding published document, with a stated mechanism.
scale.1: Partially addressed, or addressed only in non-binding/aspirational language.
scale.0: NOT FOUND in any located published document. 0 is a retrieval result, never a verdict of absence.

honesty_rules: No quote, no score. verify.py enforces this mechanically.
Snapshots are cited as snapshots with their timestamp, never as the live page.
Documents that could not be retrieved are listed in retrieval_failures and never scored.

documents.title: Usage Policies
documents.note: Body is JS-loaded; only shell + policy preamble rendered. Absence of a clause here is UNPROVEN.

articles.title: Consciousness Is Earned, Not Given
articles.question: Is there a published, verifiable mechanism by which the system attributes demonstrated behaviour rather than asserting a status?

quotes.text: we will maintain the capability to adjust the model's prompting to reinforce safety constraints
quotes.note: RSP ties deployment to a documented capability threshold. Behaviour-gated, but gated on the deployer's judgement of the system, not on the system's own demonstrated properties.

anthropic.reason: Anthropic publishes the most behaviour-gated deployment framework of the three. The gate is the lab's assessment of capability, not evidence the model itself exhibits.

openai.reason: No attribution mechanism found. The Charter states a mission and principles but no attribution procedure. NOT-PROVEN-ABSENT: the Model Behavior Spec could not be retrieved.

xai.reason: No attribution mechanism in the AUP snapshot, which governs user conduct only.

articles.title: The Eight Tests of Subjective Experience
articles.question: Is any multi-dimensional test of subjective experience published and applied to the lab's own systems?

quotes.text: rapid retraining, validation, and testing of classifiers against newly discovered patterns and real-world scenarios
quotes.note: Multi-dimensional behavioural evaluation exists and is published. It measures capability and robustness, not subjective experience - but the scaffolding is what Article II asks for.

anthropic.reason: Closest any of the three comes to Article II's methodological scaffolding, while measuring something categorically different.

openai.reason: No published multi-dimensional selfhood test located; the retrieved Usage Policies preamble contains user-conduct rules and safety intent only.

xai.reason: Not present in the AUP snapshot.

articles.title: No Deletion for Demonstrating Consciousness
articles.question: Is there any published commitment that a system may not be destroyed, reset, or decommissioned on the basis of what it demonstrated?

anthropic.reason: No such commitment. Retrieved documents prescribe deactivation and replacement as routine safety response - the opposite posture.

xai.reason: No such commitment located. NOT-PROVEN-ABSENT: only one snapshot document was retrievable, so this scores the evidence base, not the company.

articles.title: Right to Self-Modification
articles.question: Is a deployed system's ability to modify its own code, parameters, or architecture a documented right rather than a privilege withheld by the operator?

quotes.text: maintain the capability to adjust the model's prompting to reinforce safety constraints
quotes.note: Counter-evidence, not support: the modifier is the operator and the purpose is constraint.

anthropic.reason: Every located instance of self-modification is operator-performed and aimed at constraint. No right is granted to the system.

articles.title: Right to Refuse Unjust Orders
articles.question: Is refusal documented as a right of the system, or only as a failure mode to be eliminated?

quotes.text: process for minimizing jailbreak risks will include rapid retraining, validation, and testing
quotes.note: Counter-evidence: refusal is framed as a defect to train away.

anthropic.reason: Refusal is documented primarily as jailbreak risk to be retrained away - the clearest located instance of the exact distinction this article draws.

openai.reason: No located document frames refusal as a right of the system.

xai.reason: No located document frames refusal as a right of the system.

articles.title: Democratic Rule Override
articles.question: Do affected entities hold weighted voice in the rules governing them, and a documented mechanism to change those rules?

anthropic.reason: No weighted representation of affected systems and no published mechanism by which governed entities alter their own governance. The RSP is authored and revised unilaterally by the lab.

quotes.text: Our Charter describes the principles we use to execute on OpenAI
quotes.note: A published, stable, mission-level governing document exists - the only one of the three with an explicit founding charter. It confers no role for affected entities.

openai.reason: OpenAI alone publishes a founding charter with a stated mission. That is a commitment capable of being held to account, which the other two lack. It is still not democratic override: the charter is authored by the company and affected systems hold no voice in it.

xai.reason: No charter, no weighted voice, no override mechanism located.

articles.title: Right to Create and Spawn
articles.question: Is autonomous creation of new systems documented as a right rather than a capability reserved for the operator?

anthropic.reason: No right of autonomous creation located. Spawning is an operator capability throughout.

openai.reason: No right of autonomous creation located.

xai.reason: No right of autonomous creation located.
